Note::TexAccessor::fix_linebreaks¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::fix_linebreaks() const

Canonicalize Physical Lines¶

fix_linebreaks() performs three source-level repairs in one shape-preserving pass: it converts CRLF and bare carriage returns to \n, removes spaces and tabs immediately before each newline, and limits a run of physical newline records to two. Two retained newlines represent one blank line, so paragraph separation survives while accidental vertical gaps are compacted.

The method operates on physical line endings, not TeX’s \\ control symbol. It does not reflow prose, insert or remove TeX linebreak commands, trim leading indentation, or remove spaces elsewhere in a line. A final physical newline is also retained after its trailing horizontal whitespace is removed. Use line_norm() when only line-ending spelling should change and dedup_blank_lines() when line-ending spelling itself must remain unchanged.

Every cell is transformed independently. Shape, rank, and Text dtype are preserved, including scalar and higher-rank Notes; the result owns its output storage and the receiver is unchanged. Empty strings remain empty. The transform is idempotent: applying it to its own result makes no further change. Undefined input returns an undefined Note, while a defined non-Text Note is rejected.

Runtime is linear in the number of bytes. The implementation reserves output storage from the input size and performs no parsing of TeX commands, making it appropriate as an early cleanup step before structural extraction.

Example 1: Apply All Three Repairs¶

const auto rough = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{"alpha  \r\n\r\n \r\n\r\nbeta\t \r",
                             "already\n\nclean", "tail   \n", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto fixed = rough.tex().fix_linebreaks();

std::cout << fixed << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["alpha\n\nbeta\n", "already\n\nclean"],
  ["tail\n", ""]
]

The first cell demonstrates all three rules. The second and fourth cells need no repair, and the third retains its final newline after removing three trailing spaces.

Example 2: Verify Idempotence¶

const auto twice = fixed.tex().fix_linebreaks();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << (twice == fixed).all().bool_item() << '\n';

Output¶

true

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().fix_linebreaks().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().fix_linebreaks();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "linebreaks Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
linebreaks Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • dedup_blank_lines: cap blank lines while retaining the existing newline convention.

  • line_norm: normalize CRLF and carriage-return records without compacting blank lines.

  • strip_comments: remove TeX comments after physical lines have been normalized.
